notes: Shared harness p95 table (operator ruling §7c.34), implemented and landed. One published table — docs/infra/harness-p95.md — now carries the per-family wall-time distribution (n, p50, p95, p99, max) and the fuse threshold (ceil(3 x p95)) for pi (deepseek), claude and ollama, with the population rule verbatim and the exclusions actually applied. BOTH fuses read it: T634's claude liveness fuse and T643's pi/ollama progress fuse now derive their threshold from the table (no fuse derives its own denominator privately again). The table is regenerated by `tools/runner --recompute-harness-p95` (deterministic: byte-identical twice, wired as a regression), NOT recomputed at read — argued in the doc: untracked/runs/ is host-local and does not survive a clone, so a recompute-at-read fuse would have no population (and a different threshold) on every other host; a fuse threshold must be reproducible across hosts, and only the committed table gives that. The pi/ollama progress sensor now additionally counts the declared deliverables' mtime (T643's landed half): a lane writing its deliverable is making progress whatever its stream says. Snapshot at commit e890b5a: pi n=75 p95=2415.08 -> 7246 s (was 600 s flat); claude n=36 p95=1505.15 -> 4516 s (was hardcoded 4631 s); ollama n=9 p95=2255.02 -> 6766 s. The five known watchdog/liveness kills are absent from the p95 population and each survives the new threshold: T526 (pi, 1129.6 s) +6116.4 s, T635 (pi, 1732.6 s) +5513.4 s, T638 (pi, 1901.3 s) +5344.7 s, T616 (claude, 600.8 s) +3915.2 s, T643 (pi, 1706.8 s) +5539.2 s.
